text:
anya: FYI onboarding smoke for polaris9b (llama->gemma-style convert) shows weird token-drop on long prompts after int8 dynamic quant. observed missing numeric slots in timeline outputs.

mike: missing as in truncated tokens or replaced with <unk>?

anya: replaced with plausible but wrong values, not <unk>. e.g. input contained 'Q1 2025' and model outputs 'Q3 2024'. appears correlated with runlength > 1024.

yvette: could be rotary offset wrap or a token-id remap that splits 'Q1' vs 'Q' '1'. Did converter change token IDs for the quarter tokens?


tom: quick repro:
```
$ python ./tools/run_infer.py --model polaris9b-int8 --prompt-file tests/long_timeline.txt --max-len 1536
# look at outputs around 1200-1300 tokens where numeric slots live
```
Got 3/10 mismatches on our timeline-checker.

anya: tokenizer check:
```
>>> tok.encode('Q1')
[1209]  # fp16 bundle
>>> tok.encode('Q1')  # int8-converted bundle
[12, 98]
```
Yep, split in converter. there is a "split_compound_tokens=true" flag in convert logs.

mike: splitting compound tokens can shift positional baking for rotary since token count changed. for long contexts small shifts stack up and you can hit phase wrap in later layers.

qa-bot: regression test: timeline-checker v2 reports 30% more slot drift vs fp16 baseline for prompts > 1024 tokens.

yvette: two parallel triage paths: 1) revert token split to preserve compound tokens; 2) keep split but adjust rotary positional bake: apply phase-shift offset table at export or use rotary_scale per-layer.

tom: I can try per-layer rotary_scale anneal: higher layers damped to 0.88, lower layers 1.02. script:
```
python tools/export_rotary.py --model polaris9b --per-layer-scale "[1.02]*6 + [0.98]*6 + [0.88]*6" --out polaris9b-int8-rotary-tweak
```

anya: also want to test KV warmstart: copy fp16 KV projection weights into int8 runtime for first 8 layers to see if attention state initialization reduces drift.

mike: note: per-layer scaling and kv warmstart are orthogonal. run both combos but keep runs small: our dev-gpu cap is 3 heavy jobs (ops-bot).

ops-bot: Scheduling note 1: only 3 concurrent heavy quant jobs allowed on dev-gpu today; estimated queue time ~2h if more queued.

anya: plan: schedule 6 runs: (token-split revert + int8 baseline), (token-split revert + int8 + kv-warmstart), (split + per-layer-scale), (split + per-layer-scale + kv-warmstart), plus two sanity fp16 vs int8 baseline runs. I'll label runs and attach seeds. link: https://runs.redwood.local/plan/polaris9b-int8-longctx-8280000001

yvette: minor thought: numeric tokens sometimes have special normalization in tokenizer normalizer pipeline (e.g., 'Q1 2025' -> 'Q1' '\u2013' '2025'). check if normalization step ordering changed during convert.

mike: found converter log snippet: "tokenize_passes: [norm, split_compound_tokens, remap_ids]". original pipeline had split_compound_tokens disabled. looks like a default changed. reverting should be quick.

anya: great. queuing runs now. will paste example diffs when runs finish. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

qa-bot: once runs complete, I'll auto-generate slot-diff CSV and post regression heatmap in this thread.

anya: perfect. if token revert fixes most errors, we'll do a one-off re-export and update onboard checklist to assert 'compound_token_preserved' for future converts.
